notes:
SCENARIO: utm_data jsonb persistence across variations on POST http://app.lvh.me:5007/api/v1/sign_up (password #create), no `name` key sent (first_name/last_name only). Cleanup + seed default-user-and-org.json ran clean (29 steps). HEAD fc3f047f9, branch attribution-work-qa, server up (health / -> 200). Did 4 real HTTP POSTs (fresh emails, ts=1784599686), all returned HTTP 200 and created a User (ids 39377-39380); then verified each created User's utm_data via test_frr login-shell form. Controller path: Api::V1::RegistrationsController#create -> sign_up_params permits `utm_data: {}` (registrations_controller.rb:310), mass-assigned to new User.

CASE A multi-key {utm_medium:'cpc',utm_term:'kw',utm_content:'ad1',utm_id:'x'} (id=39377): utm_data.inspect = {"utm_id"=>"x", "utm_term"=>"kw", "utm_medium"=>"cpc", "utm_content"=>"ad1"}; class=Hash; key classes=[String]; value classes=[String]; EQUAL? to string-keyed expected = true (order-insensitive Hash ==; postgres jsonb reorders keys but that is standard jsonb, not corruption). After u.reload from DB still Hash with identical values -> jsonb persisted, not just in-memory. utm_source="src_a" utm_campaign="camp_a" internal_ref="ref_a" (raw).

CASE B single-key {utm_medium:'email'} (id=39378): utm_data.inspect = {"utm_medium"=>"email"}; class=Hash; keys=[String]; EQUAL? = true. utm_source/campaign/internal_ref all nil.

CASE C special-chars {utm_term:'a b&c=d',utm_content:'123'} (id=39379): utm_data.inspect = {"utm_term"=>"a b&c=d", "utm_content"=>"123"}; class=Hash; keys=[String]; values=[String]; EQUAL? = true. Space, `&`, `=` stored RAW inside string value; '123' stored as String "123" (NOT coerced to Integer). Round-trip intact.

CASE D adversarial: utm_data sent as JSON scalar string "notahash" (id=39380): HTTP 200, user created, NO crash. utm_data.inspect = nil; class=NilClass; utm_data.nil? = true. The `utm_data: {}` strong-params permit dropped the non-hash scalar, leaving the column nil (NOT {}), exactly as spec requires.

CONCLUSION: No jsonb corruption, no key-type change (every case String keys + String values), normal multi-key persists correctly and survives reload, absent/invalid utm_data -> nil not {}. All spec behaviors confirmed. No HIGH/BLOCKER. Scripts: /tmp/l3r2a6/{a,b,c,d}.json (POST bodies), /tmp/l3r2a6_verify.rb (verification).
